data_fields.name: sync_mode
data_fields.donor_constant: ST_SYNC=0 (phase 0) or ST_RAND (random phase), per model

data_fields.name: clip_pose_end_times
data_fields.donor_constant: running end time per slot inside one cycle; cycle = last value (reader convention, inferred)

data_fields.name: clip_slot_min_duration
data_fields.donor_constant: each stored slot value must be above 0

best_idea: Let the client derive a looping creature pose from one shared clock plus a per-creature random phase, so the server sends only which clip and from when, and idle creatures do not move in lockstep.
decision_why: The client-only timing and the game-code choice of clip fit our server-authoritative split, but hit windows and kills must come from server time and the same clip data, never from the drawn pose; sync_mode is a per-creature-type flag in our catalogue (row 21) and is listed as zone data only so a zone can override it for a placed group (our proposal, not a donor fact).
acceptance: In one zone with 12 idle creatures of one type, idle poses are visibly out of step (phase spread up to 1 s); and a server test with a client clock 300 ms ahead or behind gives the same hit result for the same swing, because the window is computed from clip data and server time.
